findings.summary: The HTTP dependency loggers expose credentials despite the helper’s no-echo guarantee.
findings.evidence: src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:108 and src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:115; tests/unit/sdk/test_http.py:227; accepted docs/adr/0026-plugin-layout-and-reusable-core.md:33; ENG-EVID-3, ENG-BOUND-3; contract acceptance 1. Reproduced without sockets using the actual httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport and httpcore.AsyncMockBackend at root DEBUG: a response X-Echo header containing a synthetic credential is included verbatim in httpcore.http11 receive_response_headers.complete; a credential ending in newline appears in send_request_headers.failed; malformed response bytes appear in receive_response_headers.failed. Separately, a response reason_phrase containing the canary appears in the httpx INFO request log even with MockTransport. Sanitizing the exception after send cannot remove these already-emitted records. The current no-echo test bypasses httpcore and does not exercise these cases; dependency logging must be made safe and covered.

findings.summary: Request construction can raise an unsanitized exception containing the complete credential.
findings.evidence: src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:111; accepted docs/adr/0026-plugin-layout-and-reusable-core.md:33; ENG-EVID-3, ENG-BOUND-3; contract acceptance 1. Reproduced post_json with an ordinary AuthContext placing Secret("review-synthetic-credentialé") in X-Api-Key. http.build_request raises UnicodeEncodeError before the protected send block; repr(exc), exc.args and exc.object contain the entire credential. No request is sent. The advertised safe exception boundary must include header encoding/request construction, and tests must inspect this failure as well as send failures.

findings.summary: Malformed 4xx responses now turn an uncertain operation outcome into KnownNoEffectError.
findings.evidence: src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:143 and src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:145; src/e_agent/adapters/odoo/client.py:80; src/e_agent/adapters/odoo/executor.py:348 and src/e_agent/adapters/odoo/executor.py:353; harness/state/1/handoffs/1d.7b.json:24; ENG-TRUST-5, ENG-PLAN-3; accepted docs/adr/0026-plugin-layout-and-reusable-core.md:33. In-memory comparison with the client loaded from git show 0972f1b:src/e_agent/adapters/odoo/client.py, through the unchanged executor: HTTP 409 with JSON ["E_AGENT_CONFLICT: identity already reserved"] changes AttributeError to KnownNoEffectError(REJECTED); {"name": ["E_AGENT_CONFLICT"]} changes TypeError to KnownNoEffectError(REJECTED). The fallback loses the information needed to decide whether a prior operation committed, and bypasses the executor’s identity-code reconciliation branch. The handoff ruling that 4xx alone justifies this change is unsound. Preserve ambiguity when the provider rejection cannot be reliably classified, with executor-level regression coverage.

findings.summary: AuthContext does not reliably control the credential ultimately sent on the wire.
findings.evidence: src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:101, src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:105 and src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:115; tests/unit/sdk/test_http.py:86; harness/state/1/handoffs/1d.7b.json:3; ENG-WORK-2; task 1d.7b AuthContext acceptance and accepted ADR 0026 common-SDK amendment. Reproduced with MockTransport: caller headers={"authorization":"Bearer attacker"} plus AuthContext placement Authorization yields two Authorization values, attacker first, rather than replacing the caller value. Also, base_url="https://user:password@good.example" causes httpx.send to replace the applied Bearer credential with Basic dXNlcjpwYXNzd29yZA==. Normalize credential header replacement case-insensitively and prevent implicit URL-userinfo authentication from superseding the AuthContext; the existing test covers only identically cased header keys.

findings.summary: Auth placement can inject a different Host after the host guard has already passed.
findings.evidence: src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:102, src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:105 and src/e_agent/sdk/http.py:112; src/e_agent/sdk/connection.py:22; ENG-WORK-2; contract acceptance 1 and accepted ADR 0026 common-SDK host-pinning requirement. Reproduced with a valid AuthContext placement {"header":"Host","prefix":""} and synthetic secret "evil.example": post_json to https://good.example/x sends Host: evil.example without HostNotAllowed. The request URL origin stays good.example, so the subsequent URL-only check does not detect the different HTTP authority and a shared ingress can route to another virtual host. Validate the effective headers after auth application and request construction, or reject routing-header auth placements. This is an HTTP authority bypass, not evidence of a changed TCP destination.

findings.summary: The plugin dependency conformance check ignores forbidden dependencies in optional extras.
findings.evidence: tests/conformance/test_plugin_dependencies.py:49 and tests/conformance/test_plugin_dependencies.py:51; ENG-WORK-2; contract acceptance 2; docs/adr/0026-plugin-layout-and-reusable-core.md:30. Reproduced with an in-memory Path.read_text wrapper only (no file edit): append [project.optional-dependencies] forbidden = ["e-agent-kernel>=0.1,<0.2"] to the Odoo pyproject text. test_plugin_dependencies_are_the_common_base still passes and reports 3 plugins. Installing that extra would introduce a forbidden e-agent dependency while this promised distribution guard stays green. Include optional dependency groups in the scan and a negative test through the manifest/config reader, rather than testing only already-normalized PluginDist objects.
